Fourteen years.

Fourteen years was how long creative works were protected under the original copyright acts. Owners could apply for a one-time extension of fourteen additional years, after which creative works entered the public domain. That's the social contract under which "copyright" was sold to the masses.

Now we have intellectual property that is "protected" throughout the life of a creator, with a seventy year exclusivity granted to the estate or other copyright owner, and decades-long extensions to this postmortem term granted so regularly that we no longer have anything entering into the public domain that isn't specifically released into it. That's not the way this is supposed to work. At all.
